@Edison Xie and I host a casual online workshop every Friday at 14:00 CET (20:00 UTC+8). As the name suggests, we work on removing set_option from Mathlib and opening PRs to reduce technical debt. In each session, attendees propose Mathlib files containing set_options, and we discuss together how to remove them. We usually run small experiments to redesign or improve old definitions, building on new knowledge such as transparency.

We have opened #44421, #44272, and #44192 as results of this workshop, refactoring HomologicalComplex.op and PAdicInt.

If you'd like to join, please contact @Edison Xie or me. @David Ang, @Nailin Guan, and @Tingxiao Shi attended last time.

If everyone in the workshop understands Chinese, we speak Chinese—which is why it's currently referred to as the "remove set_option Chinese workshop" in the above PRs. But we'll switch to English if anyone else joins :)

This week we'll be focusing on docs#RestrictScalars and docs#ModuleCat.restrictScalars, in particular we'll try making it an one-field structure and experiment on its behavior!
This is an interesting topic! Is @Nailin Guan involved? He has been thinking about change of scalars recently.

The first thing to try would be to make these definitions implicit_reducible or @[reducible] def.
One difficulty with automation (whether this is for the restriction or the extension of scalars) is that restrictScalars takes a RingHom as a parameter, while RestrictScalars relies on an Algebra instance, which means that one may have to algebraize a RingHom into an Algebra instance in order to be able to do computations.
